[h1]Sixteen Years Later, Still Setting the Standard[/h1]

After more than [b]530 hours[/b] with Civilization V, I still consider it one of the finest 4X strategy games ever made. Its enduring appeal lies not in any single mechanic, but in how successfully its systems work together.

[b]For me, Civilization has always been about building an empire, not simply conquering one.[/b] Developing a prosperous economy, advancing technology, managing diplomacy, and preparing for occasional wars all contribute to a satisfying sense of historical progression. Civilization V strikes an exceptional balance between these competing priorities. Every decision feels connected to the civilization you are creating.

It is certainly not without flaws. Diplomatic behavior can be inconsistent, the AI occasionally makes questionable military decisions, and the late game can become tedious. Yet these shortcomings rarely undermine the strength of the overall experience, particularly with the Gods & Kings and Brave New World expansions.

[u][b]Civilization V versus Civilization VII[/b][/u]

Civilization VII deserves credit for attempting to reinvent aspects of the series. However, its changes to empire development create a fundamentally different experience. Where Civilization V emphasizes the continuity of guiding one civilization through history, Civilization VII places greater emphasis on adaptation and reinvention between eras.

[i]Neither philosophy is inherently wrong, but I find Civilization V's approach considerably more satisfying.[/i]

Sixteen years after release, Civilization V continues to receive remarkably positive recent Steam reviews. This speaks volumes about the enduring satisfaction players find in its design.

[b]Civilization V succeeds because it understands something fundamental: the greatest pleasure of a 4X strategy game is watching an empire develop through decisions that remain meaningful from the first turn to the last.[/b]

[u][b]Verdict: Highly Recommended.[/b][/u]

[i]Some games age. Others endure. Civilization V has earned its place among the latter.[/i]

Rating: 10 / 10

I can't have 1K+ hours in this game and not give it a 10 / 10.  Is it actually a 10 / 10?  I don't know, but I became so used to this game that when I tried Civ 6, I instantly hated it... everything was different, and I guess I got lumped in with the other mouth breathers that love 5.

This game has so much to offer, and for some reason, the progression from barbs to high class nuking society never got old.  The unique perks for each civ were fun to explore.  The automation of your workers is god level design, and you can't convince me otherwise Civ 6ers.

I will say that the enemy's naval units seems busted... as in actually busted, not in a good way; they're pretty stupid, even on Deity.  Speaking of the Deity difficulty, screw you Firaxis... you people are evil... just straight up letting the CPU cheat is so unfair and obviously difficult.

Achievement-wise, double screw you Firaxis.  Some of those Deity achievements were absolutely insane.  The only way to win was pure luck + a Beautiful Mind calculated moves down to the last turn.  I save scummed the Praise the Victories one until I won at turn 99 (of 100), and an embarrassing amount of time dedicated to that 1 achievement.  You don't feel a sense of accomplishment from it because you have to save scum to win, and that never feels great.  Other notable awful ones... Pax Romana, Red Badge of Courage, and some of those Into the Renaissance achievements.

Having said all that, it's so much fun getting to a level of experience in this game where you bully the CPU... set up a game where you can only win by domination, getting nuclear subs before the CPU on a water map, and then they eventually all turn on you at the same time and fighting them off.  Buncha babies, I got nukes, what you got?  OH YOUR STUPID PLANES/MILITARY THAT YOU PULL OUT OF THIN AIR?  Whatever, I'm over it.

I realize most of my reviews are anecdotal and scatterbrained, so you're going to have to deal with it, and take my word for it bro... this game is absolutely worth it, and sooooo much better than Civ 6.

Civ 4 is a better game. Denounce system is a joke, if one AI denounces you with in 20 turns the rest will. An Ai has been your friend since the beginning of the game? They now view you as the bad guy and there is no way around it, you are stuck like that for the rest of the game. So good luck getting any trade deals or any of the AI's to do anything remotely useful for the rest of the game if even one one of them denounces you. 
On top of that the moding seen is almost non existent, there may be some still active but most of the one I use have not bee updated in 10+ years, which make it hard to breath new life into this game. 
In sort go play Civ 4 if you want a better civ experience or 6 if you want an active moding seen.
